sources.citation: William Hirstein, V. S. Ramachandran (1997). Capgras syndrome: a novel probe for understanding the neural representation of the identity and familiarity of persons. Proceedings of the Royal Society of London. Series B: Biological Sciences.
sources.notes: Foundational primary study (1997) in Series B: Biological Sciences establishing the core experimental paradigm and quantitative parameters.

sources.citation: Max Coltheart, Martin Davies (2022). What is Capgras delusion? Cognitive Neuropsychiatry.
sources.notes: Coltheart & Davies (2022) two-factor critique explaining why fusiform-amygdala disconnection alone requires a second frontal belief-checking deficit.

sources.citation: Pedroso Vsp (2021). Capgras Delusion in the Digital Age. Psychology & Psychological Research International Journal.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2021) in Psychology & Psychological Research International Journal extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Divyanshu Bansal, Shikha Sharma, Nand Kisor Tak (2026). Capgras Syndrome with Delusion of Negation. Annals of Indian Psychiatry.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2026) in Annals of Indian Psychiatry extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: J.P. Luauté, E. Bidault (2010). Capgras Syndrome: Agnosia of Identification and Delusion of Reduplication. Psychopathology.
sources.notes: Subsequent empirical and theoretical investigation (2010) in Psychopathology extending the foundational findings.

sources.citation: Nora Breen, Diana Caine, Max Coltheart (2000). Models of face recognition and delusional misidentification: A critical review. Cognitive Neuropsychology.
sources.notes: Evaluates dual-route face-recognition models and flat skin-conductance responses to familiar faces in Capgras delusion.

sources.citation: Michael B. Lewis, Hadyn D. Ellis (2001). A two-way window on face recognition: Reply to Breen et al. Trends in Cognitive Sciences.
sources.notes: Synthesizes autonomic disconnection and two-factor belief-evaluation accounts of Capgras misidentification.
